name: Contingent Contracting
scenario: Advisory services contract where the client questions whether the consultant's predictive pipeline optimization will produce a projected 30% revenue expansion.
script: "Let us tie our compensation directly to realized performance. We will reduce our upfront advisory retainer to a baseline of $40,000; if your pipeline expansion hits or exceeds 30% by the end of Q3, our firm receives an incentive distribution equal to 25% of all incremental margin generated above that baseline."
defense: Refuse the contingency: it rewards short-term velocity over brand; require a predictable fee-for-service model.
originFull: Risk Tolerance Asymmetries and Probabilistic Belief Variances enable negotiators to bridge speculative deadlocks by creating agreements tied to future, verifiable outcomes rather than debating uncertain forecasts.
defenseFull: If an opposing party attempts to impose a high-risk contingent fee structure: "A contingency model creates perverse incentives to optimize for short-term transactional velocity at the expense of our enterprise brand. We require a predictable, fee-for-service compensation model."
